description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-force_control_task_lib-version-1.0..description:
Library force_control_task_lib version 1.0.2.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with eTaSL task specifications for force control tasks for Crospi
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

is-guarded_motion.description:
Task Specification: guarded_motion.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: Guarded motion: the robot moves along one axis (parameter axis) of the insertion frame (task_frame*tf_2_insframe) or of the robot base (world) frame until a contact force is detected. The motion is generated by force control (admittance) along x, y and z: along each axis the robot moves with a velocity K_force*(measured force - desired force)/K_F, i.e. it moves in the direction opposite to the desired force in contact_forces until that force is measured, and is compliant to external forces along the other axes (with desired force 0). The velocity along the guarded axis is limited to maxvel. The orientation is kept constant. The measured wrench is read from the input channel named by wrench_input_channel (default "wrench_input") (type wrench, expressed in FT_sensor_frame with its origin as reference point), provided by the robot driver/simulator (e.g. MuJoCo) or by a WrenchInputHandler; it is used with its own sign convention (no conversion), passed through a dead zone, compensated for the tool weight and expressed in the insertion frame with its origin as reference point. The task finishes (monitor action "exit") when, after time_delay, the absolute value of the force along the guarded axis exceeds the absolute value of force_monitor. Outputs: pose of the insertion frame (x_tf, y_tf, z_tf, roll_tf, pitch_tf, yaw_tf, task_frame_c) and the processed wrench in the insertion frame (x_force ... z_torque).
Gravity compensation (tool_weight > 0): it assumes that the force/torque sensor was tared with the tool completely vertical, pointing down (the z axis of FT_sensor_frame along gravity, -z of the robot base frame); the tool weight measured in other orientations of the tool is then compensated.

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

FT_sensor_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) of the force/torque sensor. The measured wrench of the input channel (wrench_input_channel) is expressed in this frame, with its origin as reference point

guarded_motion_frame.description: Frame whose axes define the directions of motion. task_frame: the axes of the insertion frame (task_frame*tf_2_insframe), which move with the robot. world_frame: the axes of the robot base (world) frame, applied to the origin of task_frame. The forces are always expressed in the insertion frame, so with world_frame both frames should have the same orientation

K_F.description: Diagonal elements [N/m] of the translational stiffness, as [x,y,z] along the axes of the insertion frame, used as model of the force control: the velocity along each axis is K_force*(force error)/K_F. Lower values make the robot faster and more compliant (move more for the same force error), higher values slower and stiffer

axis.description: Axis (of the frame selected by guarded_motion_frame) along which the guarded motion takes place: the velocity along it is limited to maxvel and the force along it is monitored with force_monitor. The direction of motion is determined by the sign of the corresponding element of contact_forces

time_delay.description: Time [s] after the start of the task during which the contact monitor is disabled, to ignore forces present at the beginning (e.g. due to discrete transitions of controllers). 0 activates the monitor immediately

tf_2_insframe.description: Pose of the insertion frame w.r.t. task_frame, as [x,y,z,qx,qy,qz,qw] (position in m, unit quaternion with the real part qw last), expressed in task_frame. The forces, contact_forces and (with guarded_motion_frame = task_frame) the guarded axis are expressed in the insertion frame. The default is the identity (insertion frame = task_frame)

tool_weight.description: Weight [N] (gravity force, not mass) of the tool mounted after the force/torque sensor, applied at tool_COG, with gravity along -z of the robot base frame. The gravity compensation assumes that the force/torque sensor was tared with the tool completely vertical, pointing down (the z axis of FT_sensor_frame along gravity): it removes the change of the tool weight measured by the sensor when the tool is in another orientation. 0 disables the gravity compensation (e.g. when the tool weight is negligible, or the simulator does not measure it)

K_orientation.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the initial orientation of the insertion frame. Higher values correct orientation deviations faster

maxvel.description: Maximum absolute velocity [m/s] along the guarded axis (in the frame selected by guarded_motion_frame). The actual velocity is the one generated by the force control (see contact_forces, K_F and K_force), limited to this value

force_threshold.description: Dead zone [N] applied to each force component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. It suppresses sensor noise and offsets. 0 disables the dead zone

wrench_input_channel.description: Name of the input channel (type wrench) from which the measured wrench of the force/torque sensor is read: the varname of the input handler that provides it (e.g. a WrenchInputHandler), or the channel fed directly by the robot driver/simulator (name_expr_cartesian_wrench of the MuJoCo simulator). Change it to use another sensor or input handler

contact_forces.description: Desired forces [N] as [x,y,z] along the axes of the insertion frame, in the sign convention of the measured wrench (no conversion is applied). Along each axis the robot moves with velocity K_force*(measured force - desired force)/K_F: a non-zero value along the guarded axis generates the guarded motion (in the direction opposite to its sign; e.g. with a wrench exerted on the robot, a positive z value moves the robot along -z until it pushes with that force). 0 on the other axes makes the robot compliant (it gives way to external forces) along them

weight_max_velocity.description: Weight [-] of the constraint that limits the velocity along the guarded axis to maxvel. This constraint has a higher priority than the force control and orientation constraints

torque_threshold.description: Dead zone [Nm] applied to each torque component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. 0 disables the dead zone

weight_force.description: Weight [-] of the force control constraints along x, y and z relative to the other constraints of the same priority (constant orientation). Only matters when the constraints conflict

K_T.description: Diagonal elements [Nm/rad] of the rotational stiffness, as [x,y,z]. Currently not used by this task specification: the orientation is kept constant (see K_orientation)

weight_orientation.description: Weight [-] of the constraint that keeps the initial orientation, relative to the force control constraints (same priority). Only matters when the constraints conflict

K_force.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the force control constraints along x, y and z (inverse of their time constant): the velocity along each axis is K_force*(measured force - desired force)/K_F. Higher values react faster to force errors, but too high values cause oscillations in contact

force_monitor.description: Force threshold [N] that finishes the task: the task exits when the absolute value of the force along the guarded axis (after dead zone and gravity compensation, in the insertion frame) exceeds the absolute value of force_monitor (only after time_delay). The sign is ignored; it must be non-zero. It should be smaller in magnitude than the desired force of the guarded axis in contact_forces, otherwise the robot stops before reaching the threshold

tool_COG.description: Position [m] of the center of gravity of the tool (everything mounted after the force/torque sensor), as [x,y,z] expressed in FT_sensor_frame. Used for the gravity compensation together with tool_weight

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) that is controlled, e.g. the tool center point. The insertion frame is defined w.r.t. this frame by tf_2_insframe
